comparator.name: Bachelor Fiscal Economics
comparator.academicYear: 2026-2027 (SBE Bachelor Education and Examination Regulations 2026-2027, article 16.8 and the transitional regulations; 2025-2026 regulations compared; checked 2026-10-01)
comparator.sourceNotes: The only current official programme documents reachable from this environment are the SBE Bachelor Education and Examination Regulations (BSc-EER) 2026-2027 and 2025-2026 and the UM minors page for the programme; the UM curriculum site for the programme was not reachable, and the English programme page is a minors list only. Article 16.8 of the 2026-2027 BSc-EER states that Fiscal Economics (education and examinations partly in English and partly in Dutch) will be phased out by academic year 2027-2028: there is repeat education for year-3 courses up to and including 2026-2027 and examination-only registration up to and including 2027-2028, the transitional table for students who started before September 2024 gives examination-only participation for the first- and second-year courses in 2026-2027 with no repeat education or replacement courses from 2027-2028, and SBE cannot issue Fiscal Economics certificates from 1 November 2028. The regulations therefore contain no first-year or second-year curriculum outline for the current year and no intake route. The only complete curriculum element with EC weights is the third-year outline (semesters 5 and 6): four compulsory courses of 6.5 EC (Formeel Belastingrecht TAX2016, Privaatrecht II EBC2192, Kostprijsverhogende Belastingen TAX3015, Design of Tax Systems EBC2017), a Bachelor's thesis of 8.0 EC, and four electives of 6.5 EC or a 26-EC study abroad period, totalling 60 EC. The first- and second-year courses are named in the transitional table (Introduction to Fiscal Economics, Quantitative Methods I-III, Microeconomics, Accounting and Financial Reporting, Macroeconomics, Finance, Privaatrecht I, Economy Game, Public Finance, Accounting for Managerial Decision Making, Financial Markets, Ethics Organisations and Society, Belastingrecht voor Particulieren I and II, Belastingrecht voor Ondernemingen I and II) but their EC weights and placement are not established by the reachable current sources, so they are not encoded and no 180-EC pathway is reconstructed.

exception.reason: The normalized target is an active 180-EC Maastricht University bachelor, but the current official SBE regulations (2026-2027, article 16.8) state that the Bachelor Fiscal Economics is being phased out: no new education is offered beyond year-3 repeat education in 2026-2027, only examinations remain through 2027-2028, and degrees can no longer be issued from 1 November 2028. The regulations contain no current first- or second-year curriculum, so no current 180-EC pathway for a student starting in 2026 exists to reconstruct, and the registry's active, production-eligible status conflicts with that evidence. The reachable sources establish only a 60-EC third-year outline, and encoding it as a full programme or guessing the missing 120 EC would invent components. The target's lifecycle status must be reviewed against the university's current programme register before any UCR comparison is attempted.
exception.curriculumContext: The supported third-year outline combines Dutch formal tax procedure (Formeel Belastingrecht), private law (Privaatrecht II), indirect taxation (Kostprijsverhogende Belastingen), the design of tax systems, an 8-EC bachelor thesis and 26 EC of electives or study abroad. Earlier years are named only as transitional examination-only courses in economics, accounting, finance, quantitative methods, private law and Dutch tax law without reliable EC weights. No UCR alternative is constructed because the blocking issue is the target's current existence and curriculum, not a concluded judgment about UCR course fit.
